newsitem.title: SPAIN: GOLF-MCNULTY CANTERS TO SEVEN-SHOT TRIUMPH IN VOLVO MASTERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MCNULTY CANTERS TO SEVEN-SHOT TRIUMPH IN VOLVO MASTERS.

text.p: Mark McNulty cantered to a seven-shot triumph in the Volvo Masters at Valderrama on Sunday for his third win on the 1996 European Tour.
He fired a three-under-par 68 to surge away from a quartet comprising Jose Coceres of Argentina, South African Wayne Westner and Britons Lee Westwood and Sam Torrance.

Victory was worth 150,000 sterling ($239,500) which took the Zimbabwean to fifth place on the Order of Merit. He collected a further 39,000 sterling ($62,260) from the bonus pool distributed to the top 15 on the list after the tournament.
McNulty, who led by four shots overnight, said: "Today I felt if I shot 69 someone would have to shoot 64 to beat me. That's just not on around here."
He said he settled his nerves with a seven iron to eight feet at the short third hole, from where he made birdie.
He bogeyed the seventh after a wayward tee shot. "Then when I birdied the 10th and 11th I was pretty much in cruise control and just had to avoid errors."
He holed from 10 feet and five feet for those birdies and iced the cake with a 20-foot birdie at the last.
McNulty's total of 276 was eight under for the 6,819-yard course. His earlier wins this year came in the Dimension Data Pro-am in South Africa in February and the Dutch Open in July.

Colin Montgomerie, confirmed with his first shot on Thursday as European number one for a fourth successive year, ended a run of four years in the top four by shooting 75 for 292 and a share of 29th place.
He won 8,000 sterling ($12,770) for that and a further 150,000 sterling ($239,500) from the bonus pool to boost his official earnings for the season to a record 875,146 sterling ($1.40 million).
Order of Merit runner-up Ian Woosnam shot 74 for 291 and shared 25th position. He won four times this year and earned 650,424 sterling ($1.04 million).
He said afterwards he was likely to have surgery in the next few weeks on his bad back. That would put him out of the game for three months.
McNulty described his win as "important on such a demanding golf course".
"I said to my caddy at the beginning of the week that I felt I was playing well enough to win but you can never say you can win round here. I'm very pleased with the way I've won it."
Coceres, who shot a round of 18 pars on Saturday, had a more erratic 71 on Sunday with four birdies and four bogeys on his card.
Torrance, also second here last year as he finished second on the 1995 Order of Merit, was delighted with his two closing 68s.
They boosted his bid for a ninth successive Ryder Cup appearance on this same Valderrama course next year.
